findings.title: Console sprites are padded grid cells, so centring and quarter-turning them misplaces the art
findings.claim: The spec says to centre the console sprite on the desk rectangle and turn it in quarter turns (spec L32). The imported machines and stations sheets do not have one frame per cell, though. Each frame sits at the top-left of a cell as big as the largest frame on that sheet. The manifest can only slice a uniform frameW x frameH grid and has no per-frame size or trim, so the texture an implementer gets for `console.<kind>` is the whole padded cell, not the art. Centring or rotating that texture centres the transparent cell, not the console.
findings.evidence: spec L26-32. art/import.json L36-70: the machines frames are 16x27, 16x23, 14x23, 16x15 and 24x14, so the cell is 24x27. The med pod (frame 4) has 13 empty rows under it, and the server rack (frame 0) has 8 empty columns to its right. art/import.json L72-125: stations frames 0-3 are 12x15, 12x15, 13x16 and 13x15 inside a 16x19 cell. scripts/art/importCore.ts:L88-94 packs each frame at its cell's top-left. assets.ts:L91-95 uses sliceGrid(frameW, frameH) with no trim. manifest.ts:L5-9: the sheet schema has frameW and frameH only. I confirmed the layout by viewing stations.png and machines.png: the art sits in the top-left of each cell.
findings.why: Every console will be off-centre by 1-13 art pixels, by a different amount per kind. A quarter turn about the cell centre moves the art again, and differently for each side. Two implementers will fix this in different ways, or not at all.
findings.fix: Choose one approach in the spec. (a) Give each console its own one-frame output in art/import.json, so the cell is exactly the art (stations frames 0-3 and machines 0, 1 and 4 become seven outputs), and bind each with `name`. Or (b) state that the renderer cuts a Texture of the frame's own w x h from the cell's top-left and list those sizes in the spec. Then define the anchor as the centre of the visible art, rotate about that point, and say how odd sizes such as 13x15 round onto the 2-unit grid.

findings.title: The crew foot anchor is 'measured at load', but the assets API has no pixel access, and 'per sheet' is ambiguous
findings.claim: The anchor y is meant to be the frame's lowest opaque row, measured once per sheet at load. GameAssets only exposes Texture objects, loaded through Pixi's path, and has no function to read pixels. Measuring at runtime would need a new canvas readback that the spec does not describe and that vitest cannot run without a DOM canvas. 'Per sheet' is also unclear: it could mean the lowest row over every frame, over the standing frames only, or a value per frame (walk frames may lift the feet).
findings.evidence: spec L21 and L50 (a unit test for 'the per-sheet foot anchor'). assets.ts:L6-15: the GameAssets interface has has, texture, animation, nineSlice and missing only. assets.ts:L26-30 and L52: textures load through the path. crewSprites.ts:L18 sets the anchor once as a constant.
findings.why: A plan subagent has to invent a pixel-readback path inside the renderer, or quietly hard-code the value, which the spec forbids. Either way the unit test has nothing clear to check.
findings.fix: Measure the row offline, either in `art:import` or by the plan author from the four PNGs, over frames 0-3 (standing). Record it as a constant (`LIMEZU_FOOT_ROW`) with a comment, or as a field in the committed manifest entry. Then test a pure function `footAnchorY(row, frameH) = (row + 1) / frameH` against that value. Remove 'measured at load'.

findings.title: The palette builder is to be 'ported' from a script that is not in the repo, with no requirement to reproduce the committed palette
findings.claim: Section 4 asks for 'the palette builder used for the checkpoint, ported to TypeScript'. The original builder is not anywhere in the repo, and art/palette-overrides.json does not exist. The spec does not give k, the iteration count, which frames feed the k-means, how 'explosion-pack colours kept exact' is decided, how roles and ramps map, or the override values. No test or criterion requires `npm run art:palette` to reproduce the committed palette.json.
findings.evidence: spec L45 and L50. A Grep for buildPalette, k-means, palette-overrides and art:palette finds only the spec, the brief and palette.json. palette.json:L3 describes the method in one sentence. Glob art/* returns only art/import.json. package.json:L27-30 has no art:palette script.
findings.why: A subagent who sees only the plan cannot port code it has never seen. A rebuilt builder will almost certainly produce a different 42-colour palette. The first time anyone runs `art:palette`, palette.json would change and every imported sheet would need a re-import, a silent visual change to the house palette.
findings.fix: Either commit the original builder's source, or write out the algorithm fully in the spec: k=42, the input frame set, the init, the iterations and stop rule, the exact-keep rule, and the role and ramp mapping. Write art/palette-overrides.json now with the current values from palette.json (the fire ramp, flash, lampOn, heldTick, ventSpeck, alert and breach). Add an acceptance check the owner runs locally: with the owner's asset folder, `npm run art:palette` leaves palette.json byte-identical (git diff empty).

findings.title: The 'down' console strip is said to use the failed role, but today's strip is WARN red and the new failed role is khaki
findings.claim: The spec says a down console draws 'the existing screen strip in the `failed` role'. The existing strip is not drawn in the failed role: it uses SCREEN_DOWN = WARN, a red. Meanwhile the new palette's `failed` role is #c3bc6d, a yellow-khaki. One implementer keeps the existing red strip, another uses ROLE.failed and draws a khaki strip that does not read as failed.
findings.evidence: spec L33. consoleModel.ts:L13: SCREEN_DOWN = WARN. theme.ts:L7: WARN = 0xff5b4a. palette.json:L75: "failed": "#c3bc6d". effects.ts:L92 already uses ROLE.failed for failed tiles. The override list at spec L45 does not include `failed`.
findings.why: The two parts of the sentence contradict each other. The khaki colour also suggests that mapping roles from the old palette moved `failed` away from red, which affects every failed-tile overlay as well.
findings.fix: Say 'the existing SCREEN_DOWN (WARN) strip', or add `failed` to the palette overrides with a red taken from the packs and use ROLE.failed for both the strip and the failed tiles. Choose one of the two.

findings.title: Blasts need assets and the hit signal in the same module, and no module has both today
findings.claim: The hits and the duel's random smoke tile exist only inside interiorFeel.onHit. createInteriorFeel takes no assets. The effects layer has the assets but never sees hits. The spec places blasts in `effects.above` and plays them on the presentation clock, but does not say which module owns them, how they get textures, or how frames advance. A Pixi AnimatedSprite runs on the Pixi ticker: freezeAnimations stops it only during a hitstop, and nothing stops it during a pause, so it would not 'hold while paused'.
findings.evidence: spec L39-40. interiorFeel.ts:L81: opts are { world, band, feel } with no assets. interiorFeel.ts:L116-136: onHit is private, and L126 draws the duel tile from emitter.random without exposing it. interiorFeel.ts:L145-148: a pause holds the clock, but freezeAnimations runs only on clock.stopped (the hitstop). effects.ts:L20: createEffectsLayer(assets, memory). renderer.ts:L68-69 and duel/interiorView.ts:L58-59: fx.above is added inside effects.above.
findings.why: Implementers will either add assets to createInteriorFeel, or expose a hits list from it, or re-detect hits in the effects layer, which would draw the duel tile again and pick a different tile. Each builds different frame timing too. The 'held at presentation dt 0' test cannot be written until this is settled.
findings.fix: State that interiorFeel owns the blasts. createInteriorFeel gets an optional `assets` (or the two GameAnimation values). onHit pushes a blast { name, x, y, start: clock.t }, reusing the tile it already picked for the duel smoke. Each frame, draw sets Sprite.texture to frames[floor((clock.t - start) * fps)] (plain Sprites, not AnimatedSprite) and removes the blast after the last frame. The blast sprites go in fx.above under the flash.

findings.title: Blast placement, size, count and cap are underspecified
findings.claim: Several details are left open. 'The hit room's centre tile' has no single answer for even-sized rooms (2x2, 2x1). The scale and anchor are not given (32 art px at 2x covers 2x2 tiles). A sector hit can list several rooms, while the test says 'one per hit'. It is unclear whether the cap of 4 is shared between room blasts and breach sparks. The draw order relative to the white flash is not given.
findings.evidence: spec L38-40 and L50. interiorFeel.ts:L129-133 loops over hit.rooms, so one hit can cover several rooms. sources.ts:L166-170: breach openings come from draw, not from onHit.
findings.why: Two implementers will place and count blasts differently, and the scheduling tests will disagree with each other.
findings.fix: Say: one room blast per hit room, centred on the room's centroid in world units (rounded to 2), at 2x, anchor 0.5/0.5. One spark per opened breach site at the site tile's centre. One shared cap of 4, cutting the oldest. Blasts draw under the flash Graphics.

findings.title: The cursor blink and down strip, placed from the desk rectangle, will land at arbitrary spots on the console art and may be hidden under it
findings.claim: screenCursor and the down strip are positioned from deskPicture's `screen` rectangle, which is the procedural desk's wall-edge strip. On a Maru sprite that point is not the art's own screen, so the amber cursor and the red strip will float over arbitrary pixels of the sprite. The fixtures Graphics is also a child of the desk container. If consoleLayer adds its sprites with addChild after the fixtures, the sprites cover the blink.
findings.evidence: spec L33. lightsModel.ts:L62-64 (screenCursor from picture.screen). interiorFeel.ts:L170-171. consoleLayer.ts:L7-8: the container holds one Graphics. renderer.ts:L69 and duel/interiorView.ts:L59: desks.container.addChild(fx.fixtures) is called after the layer is built.
findings.why: The look gate will show stray blinking pixels, or no blink at all, depending on child order. Implementers will handle it differently.
findings.fix: With consoleArt, either skip the cursor and the down strip (show 'down' through the 60% tint plus the existing glow off), or give a per-kind screen offset inside the sprite. Say that sprites go into a child container inserted below fixtures (addChildAt 0).

findings.title: The carried torpedo at y-30 will sit on a LimeZu character's chest or head
findings.claim: The carried torpedo is drawn at a fixed 30 world units above the crew position, chosen to clear the Puny sprite. A LimeZu frame is 16x32 art px at 2x (64 units tall), feet-anchored, and its figure is much taller than a Puny figure. The spec claims the size change is safe but does not revisit this offset.
findings.evidence: crewSprites.ts:L36: `y * TILE_PX - 30 // held overhead, clear of the sprite`. manifest.json:L174-175: Puny frames are 32x32 with feet at anchor 0.75. spec L21.
findings.why: An ordinary Coop-ii torpedo carry would draw the torpedo across the character's body.
findings.fix: With crewArt, set the carry offset from the measured head row: (footRow - headRow) * 2 + a margin. Add it to the unit tests. Also check callout and label offsets that assume a 1-tile crew.

findings.title: Downed pose: the pivot, turn direction and reset are unspecified
findings.claim: 'The standing s frame turned a quarter turn' does not say clockwise or anticlockwise, or which point to rotate about. With the foot anchor (x 0.5, y about 1), a 90-degree turn swings a 64-unit-tall body two tiles sideways out of the crew's tile. The spec also does not say that rotation resets to 0 when the crew member gets up.
findings.evidence: spec L20. crewSprites.ts:L73 (anchor set once at creation) and L81 (the downed branch).
findings.why: A downed crew member can end up drawn across a wall or in the next room, and a revived one can stay rotated.
findings.fix: Specify: rotate +90 degrees (clockwise) about the body's centre, by temporarily setting the anchor to 0.5/0.5 and placing the sprite at the crew position. Restore the foot anchor and rotation 0 on any other state. Add a unit test.

findings.title: The seated facing needs the console's wall side, which the crew layer does not have
findings.claim: Seated crew 'face the console's wall side'. The crew layer only knows Seated.station. The side is computed only inside consoles(), once per console group and keyed by members[0]. Seats at a non-first group member, such as the Skiff's Ops, need a member-to-console lookup. The spec also says nothing about draw order at an s-wall console, where the crew (drawn above the console layer) will stand in front of a console that is south of them.
findings.evidence: spec L20. crewSprites.ts:L82 (only Seated.station is read). consoleModel.ts:L69-80: the side is per group, and `members[0] !== i` skips the other members. renderer.ts:L68: consoleDesks is drawn before crew.
findings.why: Implementers will either recompute wall distances in the crew layer or call consoles() per frame. A missed group lookup gives a wrong facing or a crash on an undefined lookup.
findings.fix: Specify a pure helper `consoleSideOfStation(state): Side[]` built from consoles() (each member maps to its group's side), cached by layoutHash and passed to or computed in the crew layer. State that s-wall overlap is accepted for now, or that crew seated at an s-wall console draw below the desk.

findings.title: Paid manifest entries for LimeZu and Pimen lack the store URLs, dates and the Pimen credit the validator requires
findings.claim: The manifest rejects a paid entry unless it has a source URL, a retrieved date and a credit line. The spec gives only LimeZu's credit line. It gives no LimeZu or Pimen store URL, no purchase date, and no Pimen credit line, and it does not confirm Maru-98's or Pimen's licence terms (whether credit is required and whether redistribution is allowed inside a built app).
findings.evidence: spec L17, L26 and L38. manifest.ts:L44-51: paid entries need an http source, `retrieved` and `credit`. manifest.json:L545-551: only the Maru entry exists so far.
findings.why: A plan subagent will have to invent URLs and dates or fail validation. Shipping in a build without checked terms is a licence risk.
findings.fix: List in the spec, for each of the three packs: the store page URL, the purchase date (2026-11-16) and the exact credit line, for example 'Explosion VFX by Pimen (pimen.itch.io)'. Note where each pack's licence text was read, or flag the Maru-98 and Pimen terms as an owner check before release.

findings.title: The `console.<kind>` naming and the console layer's signature are unstated
findings.claim: `console.<kind>` could mean the numeric StationKind (console.0), the ship-data id (console.lifeSupport) or the display name. createConsoleLayer() takes no assets today, and the spec does not say it gains a parameter.
findings.evidence: spec L26. stationKinds.ts:L2-4 (numeric kinds, the STATION_IDS strings and the display names). consoleLayer.ts:L6. renderer.ts:L63 and duel/interiorView.ts:L49 call createConsoleLayer() with no arguments.
findings.why: The names in the manifest, ASSET_NAMES, FEATURE_NAMES and the tests must all agree.
findings.fix: Use `console.${STATION_IDS[kind]}` (console.navigation ... console.doors) and change the signature to createConsoleLayer(assets: GameAssets), updating both call sites.

verified: Crew sheet frame indices: each crew output takes frames 0-3 from y=0, 24 frames from y=32 and 24 frames from y=64, all 16x32, with 24 columns (art/import.json L225-542 and the same for 07, 13 and 19). Packed row-major (importCore.ts:L89-94), they become a 384x96 sheet. sliceGrid(16,32) gives indices 0-51 in the spec's order: stand 0-3, idle 4-27, walk 28-51 (spec L17).

The station frames used for consoles match the images: stations.png frames 0-3 are the four orange consoles, and machines.png frame 0 is the tall rack, frame 1 the green machine and frame 4 the wide pod (viewed both PNGs).
Explosion frame counts: explosion-room has 14 frames of 32x32 (import.json L1574-1663), explosion-hit 11 of 16x16 (L1501-1572) and explosion-big 13 of 64x64 (L1665-1748), matching spec L38.
The new per-slot crew names (crew.p<k>.*) do not collide with the required Puny crew.* names. The manifest's no-duplicate rule (manifest.ts:L54-63) is satisfied because the names are distinct.
Boarders use only the Puny crew.idle.s, crew.idle.* and crew.walk.* names (boarderLayer.ts:L46, L58-59), so leaving them on Puny (spec L13) needs no change.
A console group's first member is well defined: consoles() emits once per group at members[0] (consoleModel.ts:L72-73), and the kind is state.derived.stationKind[members[0]] (derived.ts:L20, L61-64).
Draw order: consoleDesks sits under crew, and effects.above (which holds fx.above) sits under feel.lights (renderer.ts:L68-69; duel/interiorView.ts:L58-59), consistent with spec L40.

Fallback mechanics: optional names that are unbound or fail to load go into assets.missing (assets.ts:L74-76), and featureReady checks FEATURE_NAMES (fallback.ts:L19-21), so new features crewArt, consoleArt and blastArt fit the existing pattern.
No sim change is required by any section. The only randomness used is the presentation emitter (interiorFeel.ts:L126), not the sim RNG.
not_verified: That LimeZu rows 0-2 run right, up, left, down. The thumbnail of crew_04.png is consistent with side, back, side, front, but too small to be sure of right versus left.
The exact visible head height of the LimeZu figures, used in the torpedo-offset finding. It is estimated from the thumbnail, not measured.
